clue.text: In the US, summer gala fails to open

definitions.note: the American spelling of the adjective meaning relating to summer

indicators.note: the gala word does not get its opening letter, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a gala is a festival, a celebratory event

explanation.surface: An American summer fete is a washout from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' is the adjective here, not the season: the answer is the US spelling of AESTIVAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to the warm season, and Americans drop the A of the British spelling.

clue.text: Juicy 7?

parts.note: 7 is the theme answer, fine china; one kind of Japanese pottery shares its name with a juicy citrus fruit

explanation.walkthrough: 7 is PORCELAIN. SATSUMA is a Japanese ware, and also a small orange, so a 'juicy' piece of this porcelain is a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Satsuma ware is cream-coloured Japanese pottery, and a satsuma is also a seedless mandarin orange full of juice.

clue.text: Two glazes spoil 7

indicators.note: a glaze is a coating, so the Roman two coats or encloses the spoil word, one numeral each side

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
to mar is to spoil

explanation.surface: Applying two coats of glaze ruins a piece of pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 7 is PORCELAIN. 'Glazes' looks like the potter's craft, but it says one piece covers the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Imari is a style of Japanese porcelain, named after the port it was shipped from.

clue.text: Half-baked bun with meal — that feeds developing bird

indicators.note: half-baked means badly prepared or messed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An undercooked bun and meal, fed to a chick in the nest.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg white is the protein-rich substance that nourishes the embryo chick inside the egg.

clue.text: Gas for cooker extinguished originally

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a pan is something you cook in

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter of extinguished is used

explanation.surface: Fuel for a stove that has gone out.
explanation.definitionFit: Propane is a flammable hydrocarbon gas sold in bottles for camping stoves and barbecues.

clue.text: Vegetable put back in larder on a piece of 7, say

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts the first piece above the second
put back in means the letters found inside the larder word are turned round

parts.note: two letters taken from inside the word larder, its second and third
7 is PORCELAIN; a dish is an example of a piece of china

explanation.surface: Someone returns a vegetable to the pantry on a china plate.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'larder' backwards and the plant's first two letters sit inside it; 7 is PORCELAIN, of which a plate is a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A radish is a crisp red root eaten raw in salads, a common vegetable.

clue.text: White material cut up, one dressed in impressive style

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to crop is to cut

indicators.note: dressed in means the one goes inside, clothed by the style word

parts.note: elan is flair or impressive style
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Fine white fabric is trimmed, and someone is dressed stylishly in it.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' means the word is read upwards; 'material' suggests cloth, but the answer is a ceramic.
explanation.definitionFit: China is a fine white ceramic, so it is a white material used for cups and figurines.

clue.text: 29 potty deserved ruination

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters are scrambled; also a nod to pottery

parts.note: 29 across is MEISSEN, the German porcelain

explanation.surface: A mad piece of German china meets its just deserts.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 across is MEISSEN, whose letters rearrange to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nemesis is a downfall that someone has earned, named after the Greek goddess of retribution.

clue.text: Livingstone out of doghouse over Blairite having prioritised issue, a political icon

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the next
out of means the Livingstone name leaves the doghouse word

parts.note: a kennel is a doghouse
Ken Livingstone, former Mayor of London

indicators.note: prioritised means put first, so the issue word moves to the front

parts.note: Peter Mandelson was a close ally of Tony Blair, the UK Labour prime minister
issue means offspring, a son

explanation.surface: A Labour politician is kicked out of the doghouse while a Blairite puts something first.
explanation.walkthrough: KEN leaves KENNEL to give NEL; SON moves to the front of MANDELSON for SONMANDEL; A finishes. Ken Livingstone and Peter Mandelson are British Labour politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: The South African anti-apartheid leader and president is one of the world's most revered political figures.

clue.text: Beaten regularly, a mount

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking alternate letters

parts.note: every other letter of beaten, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Someone beaten on a regular basis by a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is a volcano in Sicily, and Mount Etna is its full name, so it is a mountain.

clue.text: Bit of a bloomer, perhaps

parts.note: a bloomer is a long crusty loaf, and a tiny piece of it is a crumb of bread

explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of a bloomer' sounds like a minor mistake; in Britain a bloomer is also a type of loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny fragment of loaf is exactly what the British loaf name bloomer would shed.

clue.text: Youngsters investing one grand in artistic movement

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so the youngsters word wraps around the one

parts.note: cubs are young animals or junior scouts
I is the Roman numeral one
M is short for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Children putting a thousand pounds into an art movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubism, led by Picasso and Braque, is an early twentieth-century school of painting using geometric forms.

clue.text: Doubt writers from America residing in outskirts of Stoke

indicators.note: residing in means living inside, so these go within the outskirts
outskirts are the edges, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Stoke
US is short for the United States
pens are writing instruments

explanation.surface: American writers living on the edge of Stoke, an English pottery town, have their doubts.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is a state of uncertainty, so it fits doubt as an anxious not-knowing.

clue.text: Damaging 7, order parts

indicators.note: parts means splits apart, so the order word separates the china word

parts.note: 7 is PORCELAIN; Ming is the Chinese porcelain from that dynasty
to align is to put in order

explanation.surface: Breaking up fine china, with an instruction to sort the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Maligning means speaking ill of someone, so it is harmful to a reputation.

clue.text: Need information covered by lists, briefly

indicators.note: covered by means the information goes inside the lists word
briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: indices are lists, such as the index of a book
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A need for information hidden in short lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigence is poverty, a state of want or need.

clue.text: Language is on flyers, written backwards

indicators.note: the whole phrase is to be written in reverse order

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, are flyers

explanation.surface: A language printed back to front on aviation leaflets.
explanation.definitionFit: Farsi is the Persian tongue, spoken in Iran.

clue.text: 7 shell in case of sapphire

definitions.note: 7 is PORCELAIN; this is an English china brand

indicators.note: in means the shell word goes inside
the case is the outside, keeping just the outer letters

parts.note: first and last letters of sapphire
a pod is the shell of a pea or bean

explanation.surface: China shell inlaid with a sapphire.
explanation.definitionFit: Spode is an English pottery firm from Stoke, famous for its blue-and-white porcelain.

clue.text: Bakery that is quiet feeding old man

indicators.note: feeding means going into, as food goes into a mouth

parts.note: pop is a word for father, an old man
i.e. is short for id est, that is
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A bakery quietly feeding a father.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling pastries, a bakery of savoury pastries in particular.

clue.text: Cheap 7, game

parts.note: bad in the sense of poor quality, shoddy
7 is PORCELAIN; Minton is a Staffordshire porcelain maker

explanation.surface: Cheap china is a game in itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock.

clue.text: Knotty skill getting computer memory erased, initially

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer
RAM is random-access memory

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter

explanation.surface: A skill gets wiped when a computer's memory is cleared.
explanation.definitionFit: Macrame is the craft of tying cord into decorative knots, hence a skill full of knots.

clue.text: Day, for example, wearing extremely offensive perfume

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the extremes go around the name
extremely means at the extremes, the end letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of offensive
Doris Day was a US actress and singer

explanation.surface: A dayly fragrance that is extremely offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Day' is not a time but Doris Day, the singer. 'Perfume' is a verb: to scent.
explanation.definitionFit: To odorise is to give a smell to something, which is what scenting does.

clue.text: Who cares if porker given pork pie?

parts.note: a sow is a pig
a pork pie is a style of flat-crowned hat

explanation.surface: Who'd mind if a pig were fed a pork pie?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pork pie' wants to be food, but it is a hat; the pig wears it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a dismissive retort meaning that something does not matter.

clue.text: Joined, head of warrior in fine 7

definitions.note: 7 is PORCELAIN; this is an English pottery brand

parts.note: wed means joined in marriage

indicators.note: in here means the warrior's head is placed within the fine word

parts.note: good means fine

indicators.note: head means the first letter

parts.note: the first letter of warrior

explanation.surface: A warrior united with fine china.
explanation.definitionFit: Wedgwood is the English pottery firm famous for blue jasperware and bone china.

clue.text: Slope on 7

definitions.note: 7 is PORCELAIN; Canton is Chinese export porcelain

parts.note: a cant is a slope or tilt

explanation.surface: A slant on china.
explanation.definitionFit: Canton ware is the blue-and-white Chinese export porcelain from the city now called Guangzhou.

clue.text: Person's bottom, wobbly seat?

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of person

indicators.note: wobbly means unsteady, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A shaky seat for one's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds at once: the last letter of 'person' plus a jumble of SEAT, and the backside is literally on a wobbly seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Nates is the anatomical Latin word for the buttocks.

clue.text: Animal with sense of fear breaking 7

indicators.note: breaking means bursting into, so the fear word splits the china word

parts.note: 7 is PORCELAIN; china is porcelain
a chill is a shiver of fear

explanation.surface: A fearful animal breaking crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinchilla is a small South American rodent with soft grey fur.

clue.text: Get a bit of ash?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a small branch of an ash tree

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ash' looks like the residue of a fire, but it is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to grasp an idea and a small woody shoot of a tree.

clue.text: A hospital department in work by the bucketload

indicators.note: in here means the department is placed within the work word

parts.note: to ply is to work at a trade
ENT is ear, nose and throat

explanation.surface: A hospital department at work handling cases by the bucketful.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplenty means in abundance, so it means in large quantities.

clue.text: 7 of ___ men in audiobook?

definitions.note: 7 is PORCELAIN; this is the German porcelain from Saxony

indicators.note: an audiobook is heard, not read, so the words are pronounced aloud

parts.note: the gap in the title Of Mice and Men is filled by mice and

explanation.surface: Porcelain from the Steinbeck novel, read aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: Fill the blank in the Steinbeck title 'Of Mice and Men'; said quickly, 'mice and' sounds like the German town.
explanation.definitionFit: Meissen is the Dresden-area factory that made Europe's first hard-paste porcelain.
